$comment: Which OPC UA statuses count as success, and what a success with a subcode looks like. Per Part 4 §7.39 severity is the top two bits: 00 is Good, 01 Uncertain, 10 Bad. A Good *subcode* — GoodClamped, GoodLocalOverride, GoodNoData — is a success that says something more. #157 found Node accepting only plain Good (a read came back null, a completed method call and an empty history range were reported as failures) while python-opcua's is_good() tests severity. Both now test severity, and report the subcode by name so nothing is hidden. Driven by BOTH tests/unit/test_status_severity.py and packages/server-node/test/status-severity.test.mjs. `code` is the status's numeric value, and both client libraries must know it by `name`.

reads.name: a locally overridden value is still the value, and says so
a clamped value is still the value, and says so
an Uncertain value is not reported as a value
a Bad read has no value

maxChange.name: a GoodLocalOverride current value is where the node is
and is measured from
maxChange.error: Moving node ns=2;i=90 from 50 to 140 is a change of 90, and the operator policy allows at most 10 in one write. Nothing was written. Make the move in steps if it is deliberate.

maxChange.name: an Uncertain current value cannot be measured from
maxChange.error: Node ns=2;i=90 has a max_change bound, which can only be checked against its current value — and reading it failed (UncertainLastUsableValue). Nothing was written.

history.name: GoodNoData with no HistoryData is an empty range, not a failure
a Bad answer is still a failure
history.error: Read history failed with status: BadHistoryOperationUnsupported
